The R2 Is Rivian's Key to Profitability, but It Won't Be Easy To Replace Tesla As the EV Champion
9 photos
Photo: Rivian
Rivian's third-quarter results showed the EV startup closer to becoming a profitable carmaker, with the R2 as the key to its future plans. Rivian also believes in its chances to match Tesla as an EV and autonomous driving champion, especially as Elon Musk's company appears to waver. But it will be a difficult road ahead, despite showing promising progress in 2026.
Many EV startups have tried to follow in Tesla's footsteps, some of them by literally copying the EV market leader's strategy. However, none of them have managed to get quite close, and many have disappeared trying to establish themselves as carmakers. There's a long list of failed companies that tried to replicate Tesla's success, including Lordstown Motors, Caboo, and Fisker.
Two EV startups are still hanging, although they're not equals. Lucid Motors has an incredible technology advantage over its rivals, but poor execution and a model portfolio that isn't fit for current market conditions have put it in a precarious position. The Air sedan will not gain any favor in a market that only wants SUVs, while the Gravity SUV is still too expensive for most EV buyers.
Rivian is further up the ladder, having recently launched its first mass-production EV that props up its hopes of becoming profitable. The Rivian R2 has shown a better-than-expected production ramp-up, with a second shift added recently at its Normal, IL, factory. The carmaker is still losing money on every vehicle it makes, but it hopes the R2 will change that prospect by the end of the year.
Rivian's third-quarter financial results look promising In the third quarter of 2026, Rivian beat Wall Street expectations on almost every metric. The EV startup reported revenue of $2.16 billion vs. $1.99 billion expected, which also happens to be a 38% improvement over Q3 2025. The better-than-expected results encouraged Rivian to revise its 2026 guidance upwards, both financially and in terms of vehicle deliveries.
Photo: Rivian The shining star is the R2 compact crossover, whose production has ramped up faster than anticipated. Although Rivian does not disclose deliveries by vehicle model, CEO RJ Scaringe told investors during the earnings call that the R2 was the company's best-selling vehicle in the quarter. Estimates indicate Rivian sold about 7,300 R2 vehicles in the third quarter, making it one of the best-selling EVs in the US.
Rivian is still losing money overall (about $8,400 per vehicle delivered), but its losses continued to narrow, with the Q3 net loss below $1 billion for the first time. Rivian reiterated that the R2 will have positive gross margin by the end of the year. However, the company must scale beyond current R2 production plans of 160,000 units in order to achieve overall profitability.
Volkswagen partnership remains key to achieving long-term objectives Although the R2 remains a crucial topic, one of the less talked-about surprises was the software revenue. The Software and Services part of the financial results has become difficult to ignore, with $605 million in revenue. Roughly $354 million came from the Volkswagen partnership, making the German carmaker Rivian's most important customer.
Volkswagen is paying handsome money to get access to Rivian's zonal architecture and software. Much has been said about this partnership, including doomsday scenarios. The latest bad news showed that Volkswagen is already hedging its software away from the Rivian partnership by planning to use Xpeng's software developed in China. This might well be true, but not to the detriment of Rivian, as Rivian's software guru Wassym Bensaid was quick to point out in a social media reply .
Photo: Rivian On the contrary, Rivian is expanding its partnership with Volkswagen, despite doomsayers. The latest change adds Rivian's AI Assistant to the deal, or parts of it, at least, according to the third-quarter shareholder deck. There aren't more details about this expanded partnership, but it sure looks like the Rivian and Volkswagen cooperation is growing, not shrinking.
This marks an important moment for Rivian, being the first part of its software stack shared with Volkswagen. The original partnership terms only included the zonal architecture and core vehicle OS. I can certainly see how Rivian's Autonomy efforts will next be on Volkswagen's radar, especially if Rivian demonstrates decent competence in this area.
Autonomous driving is the next chapter If you're in the Tesla bubble, you probably believe that nobody but Tesla could develop autonomous vehicles, and everyone else is so far behind that you can only see them with a telescope. Well, that's not very accurate, even though Tesla has an important advantage. Waymo might be further ahead in the autonomous driving game, although Tesla has been growing faster.
Photo: Rivian However, you should not dismiss Rivian as a worthy competitor in this field, even though the current state of affairs doesn't look very promising. Rivian's Universal Hands Free feature is not exactly autonomous driving, and many likened it to Tesla's primitive Autopilot feature. The next iteration of its Autonomy software promises point-to-point capabilities similar to Tesla FSD.
You can see how important autonomous driving is for Rivian, with RJ Scaringe spending an important part of the earnings call talking about it. Scaringe reiterated that point-to-point hands-free driving will launch later this year, starting with its own employees and early-access testers . Regular customers should get the same features next year, followed by the launch of Rivian's robotaxis in partnership with Uber in 2028.
How well these steps will be executed will largely dictate the success or failure of Rivian's bid to become an autonomous driving player and take on Tesla. Even though Tesla spent a lot of time polishing its self-driving software, it doesn't mean that Rivian has no chance of catching up. Let's not forget that Tesla botched its autonomous driving stack and only turned to end-to-end AI in 2023, with the FSD V12. Almost everything it tried before had to be discarded, so you could say it only has a three-year head start.
Rivian has a lot to catch up , including designing its own chips, a step it announced last year during the Autonomy & AI Day. For some reason, the EV startup still believes Lidar is worth pursuing, even though its current vehicles don't ship with the required sensors. To complicate things further, Rivian doesn't offer a timeline for when Lidar will equip its vehicles, or when the RAP1 chips will start production.

Last of the Senior Packards: 1956 Patrician Runs and Drives After 30 Years off the Road
16 photos
Photo: Craiglist
Like most independent carmakers, Packard had fallen far behind the Big Three after World War II. Unable to keep up with the times, Packard merged with Studebaker , another struggling company, in 1954. Unfortunately, things didn't work out, and Packard was shut down only four years later.
The brand also spent its final two years on the market selling vehicles based on Studebakers. The 1957-1958 models are often called "Packardbakers," and diehard enthusiasts usually consider that the last true Packards were produced in 1956.
That year was also the last one when Packard produced vehicles in Detroit. Its lineup included five models at the time. The company sold the Clipper junior line, the mid-range Executive, and a senior line that included the Patrician, Four Hundred (400), and the Caribbean. The four-door sedan you see here is part of that lineage.
One of Packard's last senior cars, the Patrician debuted for the 1951 model year as a replacement for the Custom Super Eight. The company's range-topping model, the Patrician received a mild update in 1954, before receiving an extensive redesign in 1955. The latter was approved before the merger with Studebaker.
The refresh was penned by Dick Teague and turned the Patrician into a more modern and flamboyant vehicle. It also saw the introduction of the company's iconic cathedral-style taillights and a larger V8 engine. The last Patrician rolled off the assembly line on June 25, 1956. The company built only 3,375 units that year.
This four-door sedan is one of those cars, and much like many of its siblings, it spent a long period of time off the road. The vehicle was parked for about 30 years before the current owner got it. The Patrician looks like a proper barn find, sporting a weathered exterior and having a few minor rust issues.
However, the interior is in pretty good condition. The seat frames were rebuilt, while both the fabric and foam are new. The Patrician also has a new radiator, new tires, new brakes, new carpet and headliner, new shocks, and a rebuilt power rack that hasn't been installed yet.
Fortunately, the owner got the car running and driving, replacing several driveline components, including the fuel tank, alternator, brakes, and exhaust system. The mill, by the way, is a 374-cubic-inch (6.1-liter) V8 rated at a solid 290 horsepower. The engine is obviously original.
The engine mates with a push-button Ultramatic transmission, and the Packard features power windows, power brakes, power steering, a power bench seat, and auto-leveling torsion bar suspension. It was among the most luxurious vehicles of its time.
The car still needs a carburetor setup and minor work, and it's being sold as is. The owner has been working on the Patrician for four years, and he's selling due to lack of time. The vehicle is located in Williamsburg, Virginia, and it's available for only $5,000 .

MS George Eliot Will Be the World’s First Cruise Ship Dedicated to Solo Travelers
8 photos
Photo: Riviera Travel
The cruise industry is changing on multiple levels, including cleaner fuel alternatives, re-imagined layouts, and bold visions of year-long residencies. One of the most exciting trends caters entirely to solo travelers, those who are always disadvantages when it comes to conventional tourism and hospitality.
This ship named after a prominent literary figure isn’t brand-new, but it will herald a brand-new era, that of river cruises specifically tailored for folks traveling alone. This bold and welcomed initiative comes from Riviera Travel, an operator with more than 40 years of experience in the industry and a generous fleet of both river cruise ships and yachts.
Starting in 2027, the Riviera Travel MS George Eliot ship will start hosting solo cruises exclusively. Officially, it’s never been done before by a river cruise ship, and it sounds promising. The best part of this new concept is that guests can finally say goodbye to the dreaded solo supplements. Another great aspect is that they’re looking at a full season of what Riviera Travel calls “solo specific departures”, so there’s plenty to choose from.
A solo-exclusive river cruise ship also means that each guest gets to enjoy a double cabin all to themselves, and that alone makes these voyages a luxurious experience. Plus, it means that there’s more space onboard overall, in strong contrast to the over-crowded huge conventional cruise ships, and the staff to guest ratio is also automatically higher.
MS George Eliot is 110 meters long (360 feet), it was built by Scylla AG, one of the most acclaimed European builders of modern river cruise ships, and its re-imagined layout is meant to balance privacy with sociability. After all, solo traveling isn’t about isolation, but about personal comfort, as well as the opportunity to meet like-minded people.
Every one of the suites and cabins includes an en-suite bathroom with shower, individually-controlled air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, a mini fridge, and other appliances (including a small coffee and tea station). There’s only one restaurant onboard, and it combines fine dining with informal free seating.
The Sun Deck is one of the most sought-after areas onboard MS George Eliot. It houses a splash pool, a putting green, sun loungers, and a shaded seating area. The Upper Deck houses the Riverview Kitchen, a boutique, and an observation lounge and bar. The Middle deck is all about dining – this is where guests go for delicious meals, from informal breakfasts to four-course dinners.
Riviera Travel operates both river cruise ships, which are long and low and adapted for cruising on European rivers, as well as motor yachts, specifically added for cruising the Adriatic and Dalmatian coasts. Solo trips are also available onboard the Riviera Travel yachts, and if you have been thinking about trying an European river cruise, this is the name to look for, as Riviera Travel specializes in European river cruises for American travelers.

This Vannon Sprinter Camper Van Is Small on the Outside but Surprisingly Capable on the Inside
33 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / VANNON
The smaller a camper van is, the harder it is to make it as practical as a home. Still, some builders come up with clever, space-maximizing designs that turn tiny vans into luxurious adventure machines – that's the case with the rig I'd like to discuss today.
What we have here is a project based on an AWD Mercedes-Benz Sprinter with a 144" wheelbase. It's the work of Vannon, a San Luis Obispo, California-based company specializing in ultralight, performance-driven adventure rigs. We've covered one of its projects here on autoevolution: the Vannon Roamer .
All it takes is one glance for most people to tell that this rig is a camper van – several upgrades give away its identity. For starters, the vehicle rides on Agile XD wheels wrapped in Cooper Discoverer all-terrain tires.
Vannon took things up a notch when it comes to off-road capability by fitting an Agile Offroad Pro RIP suspension kit, which comes with front and rear Fox shocks, rear leaf springs, and more.
At the front, you'll discover an FVC bumper complete with a Warn winch and Baja Designs Squadron Sport fog lights. On the opposite end, Vannon added a bumper and a spare tire carrier / ladder combo, as well as a B2 carrier with a cargo box.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / VANNON Other notable mods are running boards, a Fiamma awning, power and water connections, and a set of flares. Flares, also known as pods or capsules, are designed to increase the van width to allow you to arrange the bed inside east to west instead of the standard north to south.
Things are way more interesting on the inside. Enter, and you'll notice that the interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. However, you can use a curtain to divide the two areas for more privacy.
Regarding aesthetics, the customer opted for a more practical, rugged look to match the exterior – it has black aluminum cabinetry with bamboo faces, grey Lonseal Lonridge flooring, a slatted ceiling with recessed LED light strips, and grey walls.
Vannon replaced the stock driver and passenger seats with black Scheelmann seats. They have built-in ventilation and are mounted on swivel bases, so they can be turned around to face the back of the van. You can also attach a tabletop to a Lagun mount attached to either B-pillar.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / VANNON This front seating area continues further back in the form of an additional seat with armrests. It's attached to two L-Tracks integrated into the floor and can be easily moved front and back.
There are multiple L-Track channels running from the cabin all the way to the back of the van. This allows you to attach additional seats, tie down your items, and more.
Behind the above-mentioned seat, you'll come across a simple kitchenette featuring the essentials: a deep stainless steel sink with a rotating faucet, a drawer, and an Isotherm drawer-style fridge with a tiny freezer compartment.
You also get a "command center" for the rig's utilities and two cabinets, one of which hides a microwave oven. The distinctive detail about the cabinets is that they have a large Molle panel underneath with a built-in light.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / VANNON The command center comprises a touchscreen display for monitoring and controlling power, a thermostat for a Timberline heater, and switches for a water pump, water heater, and Wi-Fi.
You can access the SCA rooftop tent only from inside the van, by using a pass-through above the seating area. Gas struts and scissor hinges help you lift it. Moreover, it offers three zipped windows and a double-sized inflatable mattress.
On the opposite side, by the entrance, Vannon installed a single-person bench with a small backrest. Lift its hinged top, and you'll reveal a toilet. Moreover, its front panel has switches for the awning lights, garage lights, and interior lights.
As expected given the interior so far, the rear part of the living space keeps efficiency at the forefront. Vannon devised a Murphy bed setup, one of the most space-maximizing bed solutions. This part of the van can be separated from the rest of the space by using a curtain, just like in the cabin.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / VANNON You'll notice two large boxes on the sides. The one on the passenger side holds a large FVC (Flatline Van Co.) Murphy bed – it can be secured upright thanks to two gas struts and two latches. With it up, you have a ton of space to store large items, even a couple of mountain bikes.
When you're ready to go to sleep or you want to lounge, setting up the bed is super easy – you just have to lower the platform after undoing the latches and folding out the tri-fold mattress. The platform rests on the box on the other side, and the result is an almost queen-size bed. The bedroom also offers a large shelf and two reading lights.
The driver's side box offers additional surface area for meal prepping. Moreover, both boxes offer extra storage space in the form of large drawers and compartments with sliding doors, while also accommodating the rig's utility systems; there's also an air compressor.
The electrical system's highlights are a 900 Ah lithium battery bank and a 3,000 W inverter. You can travel worry-free when it comes to power thanks to three charging sources: solar power , shore power, and DC-DC charging while the vehicle's engine is running.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / VANNON As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a freshwater tank, an under-mounted greywater tank, an outdoor shower, and a Duoetto water heater. Moreover, the rear doors have Molle panels attached to them, offering additional mounting points for items.
To prevent the rear doors from slamming shut or hitting the sides of the vehicle, the company added Stop-Stay gas struts. They also make them easier to open.
All in all, Vannon created a bespoke, one-of-a-kind mobile home that, despite its small wheelbase, can comfortably accommodate four people and take them on off-road and off-grid adventures. The cherry on top is the modularity given by the myriad of L-Tracks.

Formal Six-Pack: 1970 Dodge Challenger Flaunts 6-BBL Setup, 4-Speed Manual, Rare Combo
18 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer/Raffi
In 1970, six years after the Plymouth Barracuda and Ford Mustang kickstarted the pony car segment, Dodge finally decided that it wants a piece of the action. Using the then-new E-body platform, Dodge developed the Challenger, which arrived alongside the third-generation Barracuda.
Much like the latter, the Challenger was also available as a high-performance model. It used the same R/T badge as the Charger and Coronet, while engine options included high-compression big-block powerplants plus a small-block mill. However, both the R/T version and the big-block units disappeared after the 1971 model year.
Despite its short-lived stint on the muscle car market, the Challenger developed into a highly desirable classic. The R/T version is sought-after regardless of what's under the hood, but two specific models get even more attention. The Hemi is the most obvious choice, and it's also quite rare with just 356 units out there.
Then we have the Six-Pack version, which came with the six-barrel 440-cubic-inch (7.2-liter) V8. Dodge sold 2,035 examples, including 99 convertibles and 296 units equipped with the Special Edition (SE) package . The remaining 1,640 units were regular R/Ts.
The hardtop you see here is one of those cars, but it's also a rare sight due to the color combo. This Challenger is finished in TX9 Black while sporting a white vinyl top and a two-tone white/black interior. Very formal, somewhat unusual, and pretty classy for a fully-fledged muscle car.
I should also add that the mill mates with a four-speed manual transmission, which means that this Mopar is one of only 847 units made with this drivetrain setup. If we also factor in the color combo, we're looking at a very low production figure, most likely into low two-digit territory.
I found this car while browsing Bring a Trailer, and the ad says that the Challenger spent a long time in storage before receiving a rotisserie restoration between 2007 and 2009. Although it's been 17 years since then, the Mopar still looks like it just rolled off the assembly line.
The vehicle was refinished in the original color, while the Six-Pack mill was rebuilt with a stroker kit, a Hughes Engines flat-tappet hydraulic camshaft, Hy-lift Johnson lifters, and Hughes valve springs. There's no word on current output, but it should deliver more than the factory 390 horsepower.
The original fender tag confirms that the coupe was indeed born with a white vinyl top and a white/black interior. It also shows options like the Music Master AM radio, roof drip-rail moldings, tach, and a Track Pak 3.54 rear end.
The car was taken to the 2010 Mopar Nationals after the restoration, scoring 419 out of a 442 possible points. The seller claims that some of the deductions have been rectified after the judging. This Mopar may well be a concours-ready classic now.
The Challenger R/T is under the hammer as we speak, with bidding currently at $81,000 . The auction ends in 24 hours, and it could very well go into six-figure territory. How much is this formal Six-Pack worth?

Vancini Conversions Turns a Regular Sprinter Into a Custom, Fully-Equipped Mobile Podcast Studio
26 photos
Photo: Vancini Conversions
Turning a cargo van into a mobile living space is just one of the many ways in which you can give an ordinary vehicle a new purpose. These versatile vehicles can be transformed into almost anything you want, from mobile businesses and healthcare clinics to traveling workshops and more.
Luckily, there are many van outfitters out there that are not afraid to think outside the box when it comes to creating unique conversions. One of them is Vancini Conversions, whose latest creation is a beautiful mobile podcast and event studio.
Panel and cargo vans offer a great combination of mobility, practicality, and adaptability that makes them suitable for a wide range of uses, including businesses and creative pursuits that don’t necessarily need a permanent physical location to operate. A podcast studio is something that can be set up inside a van, giving more freedom of movement and allowing you to take conversations, stories, and community voices on the road.
For those who don’t know, Vancini Conversions is a Canadian custom van conversion shop that builds one-of-a-kind van conversions for both adventure and commercial applications. The Ontario-based team has considerable experience in woodworking and van conversions, and they only work on commission, so each build is specifically tailored to the customer’s needs and aspirations. In this case, they used their extensive know-how to turn a regular cargo van into an awesome mobile podcast studio.
Photo: Vancini Conversions Built for SEIU Healthcare, a local union representing healthcare workers, this conversion is of the most unique builds to leave the Vancini shop and a great example of what’s possible when a project is specifically designed around its intended purpose.
It’s based on a 2026 Mercedes-Benz Sprinter 170-EXT and comes with a nice setup for producing content on the road, two workstations, professional recording equipment, and a robust electrical system.
The van’s exterior looks phenomenal with its custom purple wrap by Branded Wraps, and it would be hard to miss it on the road. But otherwise, the outside is very minimal. The company only installed a couple of small windows, a Flatline Van Company roof rack, a Fiamma F45S awning, and Atlas Roadcamp side steps.
All the magic happens inside, where the team at Vancini created a welcoming creative workspace. Modern materials and finishes, such as Corian countertops, laminate Baltic birch cabinetry in sleek black, Lonseal flooring, and upholstered gray walls, give it a contemporary appearance. The clear cedar on the ceiling adds a warm touch, while purple accents ties the exterior design language with the interior.
Photo: Vancini Conversions The front section is occupied by an L-shaped sofa with upholstery from Shady Lady Hamilton. Finished in purple, it provides comfortable seating for podcast guests and creates a welcoming setting for conversations and interviews. It comes accompanied by a custom-made adjustable table, while two large 55-inch LG 4K OLED TVs occupy the surrounding wall space.
These massive screens can serve as dynamic backdrops during recordings. A side table next to the sofa integrates a small Vitrifrigo fridge for refreshments and a drawer for storage.
On the ceiling, the builder installed a heavy-duty L-track system, allowing for up to three cameras to be mounted up there and positioned as needed to capture video from multiple angles.
The central area of the van is dedicated to a generous workstation with a full-width table and two chairs. Three 32-inch Dell 4K monitors are positioned around this area, with two installed on swivel mounts the side walls and another on a custom mount. One section of the table folds down to create a passageway toward the rear of the van, and an L-track for securing the chairs when on the move are also included.
Photo: Vancini Conversions Smart storage solutions are also incorporated. For instance, all the space under the front sofa is storage, and one section of the central table is only attached magnetically and can be removed to access a secret storage compartment. THis provides a perfect place for cameras, lenses, and stuff like that. A floor-to-ceiling cabinet at the back of the van adds even more vertical storage for gear and other items, while Van Essential rear-door storage bags make it easy to keep brochures, flyers, and other materials organized.
The van was designed with different lighting zones to allow owners to set the mood, and multiple wall-mounted plugs with adapters for HDMI and USB-C will allow them to charge their devices.
Behind all this, a robust electrical system keeps everything running smoothly. It includes 920Ah of heated Blizzard lithium batteries, a Victron MultiPlus-II 12/3000 inverter/charger, an Orion 50A DC-DC charger and a Victron 100/30 solar charge controller. A 400-watt solar array on the roof allows for off-grid operations. The brain of the van is a Cerbo GX MK2 with a Victron Touch 70, which provides centralized monitoring and control.
Photo: Vancini Conversions This mobile podcast studio can be used in any season thanks to a Nomadic Cooling 12V X3 Helix air-conditioner, a Maxxair 7500K roof fan for ventilation, and a 4kW Eberspächer diesel heater. There is no plumbing system inside this van.
With its stylish design, extensive equipment, and reliable power system this Vancini van conversion is expected to handle recording sessions, broadcasting, and remote performance setups successfully.

This First-Ever Double Decker Park Tiny Is an Absolute Dream
20 photos
Photo: Park Model Homes
A rose by any other name might smell just as sweet in Shakespeare's world, but with a park tiny, the packaging does a lot of heavy lifting. If you look at the newest Woodland Park Liberty model, you might even say the packaging is everything.
The Liberty, or the Timber Ridge RL-260L by its full name, is one of the most popular floorplans from U.S.-based park tiny manufacturer Woodland Park. It's designed to offer sleeping for as many as eight people and to include all the creature comforts of a traditional home, except it sits on a quad-axle oversize trailer.
As such, it's the perfect vacation lodge, wherever you decide (and are allowed) to park it. For 2027, it will be even "more perfect," thanks to a series of upgrades and add-ons that help it live like a brand new floorplan. As such, Woodland Park is also giving it a new name, calling it the Double Decker TR-260L.
One dealer is even going as far as to call it the first-ever double decker park tiny . Don't take that in an absolute sense, because there definitely are other units out there that feature an exterior double porch. But this IS the first model of its kind from Woodland Park, so claims of being the "first" aren't misleading.
Photo: Park Model Homes Like the original model, this park tiny sits on a quad-axle trailer and comes in at 36 feet (11 meters) of length and 11 feet (3.3 meters) of width, but overall length is 46 feet (14 meters) with the double 10-foot (3-meter) porch, aka the highlight of the unit. That also means that you get a double entry, through the porch and through the middle of the home.
Modifications for 2027 are more of the "upgrading" kind. The sliding double glass door that served as the main entry in the original model is now replaced by a wide but fully residential door, and the glass doors are moved onto the porch. The bedroom is still on a dropped frame construction, but it's been completely redesigned. The same for the bathroom.
You still have ample sleeping space , with as high a capacity as eight people if you also make use of the sleeper sofa in the living room and the two double mattresses in the loft. You still have a chef's kitchen with a J-bar counter that's both a breakfast bar and prep surface, a fully dry bathroom, and a main bedroom on the ground floor.
Photo: Park Model Homes In many ways, this is still the same popular floorplan, but now offered with a more entertainment-friendly features.
The two decks, for instance, are perfect for that. You can host outdoor parties or use them as personal outdoor lounges by adding patio furniture, and the upper one offers a complete bird's eye view of of whatever area you're parked at.
Unlike with other park models, you don't get a TV on either deck or stuff like fireplaces or even full outdoor kitchens. But the simple possibility of taking your meals or your parties outside, while still be close enough to your home, is a nice bonus .
Photo: Park Model Homes The layout is the same as in the previous years, with the living room at one end and the bedroom at the other. The oversize loft, now offered with black safety rails and a floating steps, spreads out over the entire bedroom and the bathroom.
Since the bedroom is on a dropped frame, you get more headroom in the corresponding section of the loft. In other words, you have two levels inside the loft, which allows you to have two double beds in there with some semblance of separation, if not actual privacy.
The first unit completed and shown in the second video at the bottom of the page shows the loft with a second smart TV, a window-mounted AC, carpeted floors, and still plenty of space to move around.
Photo: Park Model Homes The bedroom under the loft has been redesigned altogether. Woodland Park changes the disposition of the queen bed to make room for a walk-in wardrobe behind a bar door for 2027, while still offering matching nightstands, a full storage compartment under the bed, and overhead cabinetry. The wardrobe is equipped with a bank of drawers, shelves, hanging space, and even a small frosted window.
The bathroom is seeing a share of changes as well, from the new surround in the shower to the upgraded linen closet by the vanity. Being a park tiny and, as such, designed to stay parked on location, where it will be hooked up to utilities, it comes with a residential plumbed toilet.
The kitchen and open-plan living room remain unchanged though. For 2027, this park tiny is equipped with stainless steel residential appliances, laminate counters, and shaker cabinets in a new color choice. It also offers plenty of space for moving around and entertaining.
Photo: Park Model Homes Past the breakfast bar is the large living room, offered standard with a sleeper sofa and an entertainment wall with a WiFi-connected 3D fireplace and a smart TV over a wood mantle. The forward part of the trailer, so the spaces in the living and kitchen, have extra ceiling height and lots of natural light thanks to lots of glazing, including clerestory windows.
The Double Decker TR-26L offers 396 square feet (36.7 square meters) of living space across the ground-level floor, to which you add the loft and the two decks, which aren't taken into account.
The unit shown below is selling for $149,898 with everything included.

For Sale: Taco With Extra Topping, aka a 2022 Toyota Tacoma TRD Sport That Is Now Far From Stock DNA
11 photos
Photo: Garage Kept Motors / Instagram
The latest Toyota Tacoma mid-size pickup truck generation arrived in North America in 2023, after the previous iteration had been on the market since 2015, bringing with it massive changes both outside and inside.
The fourth-generation Toyota Tacoma was announced in May 2023 with the design penned by Toyota's Calty Design Research facilities in California and Michigan and a complete switch to Toyota's TNGA-F global modular body-on-frame vehicle platform, shared with the full-size XK70 Tundra. The N400 Toyota Tacoma represented a massive step compared to the third iteration, changing the chassis, the exterior and interior design, but also the powertrains.
So, gone was the 3.5-liter 2GR-FKS V6 in favor of new inline-four turbo setups, complete with hybridization for the i-Force Max versions. Since its arrival, the Toyota Tacoma was extremely well received and finished 2024 and 2025 with new sales records. Even almost three years later, the third quarter of 2026 showed the Tacoma had no signs of slowing down, with deliveries up from 205k to 215k during the first nine months of the year.
However, for sure, there are folks who don’t care about the N400 and still only have eyes for the classic style and technical specifications of its predecessor. For them, sitting proudly in the inventory of Grand Rapids, Michigan-based Garage Kept Motors , this 2022 Toyota Tacoma TRD Sport has a "collection of upgrades" to make it a capable off-road-focused machine.
This is a “well-equipped, adventure-ready pickup that combines the Tacoma’s legendary reputation for durability with an extensive collection of aftermarket upgrades.” It’s finished in Celestial Silver Metallic over a black interior and has exactly 60k miles on the odometer. The double cab model now has an “aggressive stance, upgraded suspension, and impressive list of equipment,” so it stands out in a crowd for anyone looking for off-road exploration, overlanding, and even some everyday driving.
Under the hood resides Toyota’s 3.5-liter V6 engine paired with an automatic transmission and four-wheel drive, churning out 278 hp and 265 lb-ft of torque, according to the description. The upgrades then include an OTT Overland Tailor Tuning custom computer tune and a K&N performance cold-air intake, while the suspension gets Icon 51100 upper control arms, FOX 2.5 Factory Series coilovers, FOX suspension components, additional front leveling equipment, and a ReadyLIFT 2-inch block with alignment.
There’s a rear differential e-locker, and outside reside things like the 17-inch Fuel Militia D725 alloy wheels, 315/70R17 BFGoodrich All-Terrain T/A KO3 tires, a 4 Wheel Parts factory-style front bumper, Smittybilt X20 Gen2 10,000-pound waterproof wireless winch with synthetic rope, and auxiliary Pro Comp and Baja Designs lighting. At the rear, there’s a Prinsu cab rack, Yakima OverHaul HD adjustable-height bed rack, Retrax PRO XR lockable tonneau cover, dual bed MOLLE panels, bed lighting, hydraulic hood lifts, and a high-lift jack.
Inside, meanwhile, there are aftermarket seat covers, an upgraded audio system featuring a Taco Tunes subwoofer enclosure, amplifier, and upgraded door and tweeter speakers. An Apple CarPlay dongle adds modern connectivity, while front and rear digital video monitoring and recording cameras are also on point for security. There’s also a rubber bed mat and other practical accessories, by the way.
So, how much does it cost? Well, “with its combination of Toyota reliability, four-wheel-drive capability, upgraded suspension, aggressive wheels and tires, and extensive overlanding equipment, this 2022 Tacoma TRD Sport” isn’t very cheap – the asking price is $44,900. So, what do you think – yay or nay?

Bull Meets Raging Bull in Mexico As Lamborghini Temerario Poses for the Camera
11 photos
Photo: Instagram | lambomx
Lamborghini is known as the Raging Bull due to its logo and the fact that most of its models have been named after fighting bulls, including the Temerario, whose name comes from a famous fighting bull that fought in the arena back in 1875.
The name “Temerario” translates to “fierce,” “reckless,” “fearless,” or “courageous,,” whereas “Revuelto” translates to “mixed up” or “scrambled,” and it relates to “revuelta,” which means “rebellion” or “revolt,” and also comes after a fighting bull that fought in the arena in 1880 in Barcelona, Spain. The Urus, on the other hand, comes from “Aurochs” (Urus), which is an extinct species of wild ox, the ancestor of modern domestic cattle, so the SUV hasn’t been named after a fighting bull.
With this short history lesson behind us, we will now move on to the real reason behind this story, which is a short clip released on social media by Lamborghini Mexico , which shows a bull next to the Temerario, in a rural landscape. This is the company’s local branch’s way of celebrating its 16th anniversary. Lamborghini Mexico was founded on October 26, 2010, with a dealership in Mexico City, followed the next day by the dealership in Monterey.
The footage shared at the bottom of the page is on the cinematic side of things, and it is definitely worth a watch, as it’s not everyday that one gets to see a Lamborghini and a bull in the same frame. The supercar in question features a red paint finish on the outside, sits on bi-tone Y-spoke alloys that spin around the red brake calipers, and also sports some black elements. The interior is mostly black, with some red accents, including the piping and the embroidered Lamborghini logo on the headrests, and also sports plenty of carbon fiber.
Photo: Instagram | lambomx Chances are this Temerario has come directly from Ad Personam , which is Lamborghini’s personalization division, even if the automaker’s Mexican branch hasn’t mentioned it, but then again, we could be wrong, so you may want to refrain from quoting us on that. What you can quote us on is the official specs of the supercar, which features three electric motors, two at the front, and a third one mounted between the new eight-speed automatic transmission and the V8 that replaced the old model’s V10 mill.
The latter was naturally aspirated, as you likely remember, whereas the former features twin-turbocharging, and has a 4.0-liter displacement. The ICE pumps out 789 hp (800 ps/588 kW) at 9,000-9,750 rpm and 538 lb-ft (730 Nm) of torque from 4,000 to 7,000 rpm, and the total output is rated at 907 hp (920 ps/677 kW), so the supercar pretty much wipes the floor with its predecessors, not only from a power standpoint, but also from a performance one.
It features lithium-ion battery, an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission, a liquid cooled-dedicated circuit for HV components, an aluminum frame, an aluminum body, and sits on 20-inch front and 21-inch rear wheels as standard, wrapped in Bridgestone Potentza Sport tires measuring 255/35 and 325/30, respectively. Flat-out, the Lamborghini Temerario can do 213 mph (343 kph), and it takes just 2.7 seconds to hit 62 mph (100 kph) from a standstill, the model’s official spec sheet reveals.
Photo: Instagram | lambomx Are you interested in finding out how much fuel it burns? Probably not, but the number is 22.8 mpg US (10.3 l/100 km) on the WLTP cycle combined, or 16.8 mpg US (14 l/100 km) with the discharged battery, whereas the combined carbon dioxide emissions are 252 g/km.
Lamborghini presented the Temerario at the 2024 Monterey Car Week, and the Huracan’s replacement hit the assembly line the following year. So far, a single version of this supercar is on sale, but that is about to change soon, because the company is working on the Spyder. The open-top model will feature a power-retractable roof that supposedly takes 17 seconds to lower or raise, and stows away in a special compartment behind the seats.
Chances are the Lamborghini Temerario Spyder will premiere in a few months, with deliveries probably starting sometime in 2027, right in time for summer in the northern hemisphere. The convertible will be more expensive than its fixed-roof sibling, which kicks off at just under $400,000 for the 2027 model year in the United States of America, and as you can imagine, the pricing details, as well as other aspects, will be released in due course.
Now that you know the main aspects of the Lamborghini Temerario , including its neck-snapping performance, how much it costs, and the fact that the Temerario Spyder will soon join the family, it is time to invite you to scroll down to the clip embedded below, which is something else entirely, and click the play button. And don’t forget to drop a few lines after watching the video. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Lamborghini México (@lambomx)

2026 SEMA Show • Honda Racing Releases Its First-Ever In-House Made Parts for the Civic Type R and Integra Type S
Original Owners' 1979 Camaro Z28 Gets Detailed, Wife Gets Emotional After the Transformation
41 photos
Photo: YouTube/Always More To Do
What mysterious alignment occurred in 1979 to make that single model year the absolute zenith of American pony car sales, sending both the Chevrolet Camaro and the Pontiac Firebird straight to their all-time records while propelling the third-generation Fox-body Ford Mustang into astronomical production heights not witnessed since the mid-1960s?
Between the looming dread of the 1979 energy crisis, stagflation, and federal emissions chokeholds, conventional automotive logic dictated a complete collapse of rear-wheel-drive performance coupes.
Instead, the exact opposite happened across showrooms as frantic buyers realized that the traditional, V8-powered Detroit coupe was an endangered species destined for extinction. Buyers rushed to grab style and attitude before fuel regulations erased them forever. While Pontiac moved 211,453 Firebirds, Chevrolet went all-in, establishing an unassailable high-water mark of 282,571 Camaros. Leading the entire pack was Ford sold 369,936 Mustangs in 1979, revitalized by its fresh Fox architecture
The revered Z28 moniker originated in December 1966 as Regular Production Option Z28 (go figure), conceived by Vince Piggins to homologate the Camaro for SCCA Trans-Am racing. That track-focused option code blossomed across five of the Camaro’s six generations.
Photo: YouTube/Always More To Do The high-revving first generation from 1967 to 1969; the second generation spanning 1970 to 1981, which took a brief hiatus in 1975 and 1976; the third generation from 1982 to 1992; the aerodynamic fourth generation from 1993 through 2002; and the track-bred fifth generation for 2014 and 2015. The badge was omitted on the sixth generation.
In terms of sales volume, the Z28 reached its historic peak in 1979, with an astounding 84,877 units delivered to customers. Pontiac’s own Trans Am also sold strong on the muscle side of its pony architecture, with 117,108 Trans Ams (it one-upped and upset the Z28 big time that season).
Conversely, excluding the homologation infancy of 1967 when only 602 cars left dealer lots, the lowest full-model sales year for the Z28 occurred in 1972. Plagued by an agonizing 174-day United Auto Workers strike at the Norwood, Ohio assembly plant and tightening emissions mandates, Chevrolet produced a mere 2,575 examples of the 1972 Z28.
Photo: YouTube/Always More To Do For the banner 1979 model year, Chevrolet offered the Camaro in 4 distinct trim levels: the base Sport Coupe, the youth-oriented Rally Sport, the new luxury-oriented Berlinetta replacing the Type LT, and the flagship performance Z28. The engine lineup ranged from a modest 250-cubic-inch 4.1-liter inline-6 producing 115 horsepower, through a 305-cubic-inch 5.0-liter small-block V8 with 130 horsepower, up to the four-barrel 350-cubic-inch 5.7-liter V8.
Transmission duties were handled by standard 3-speed manuals, Borg-Warner 4-speed manuals, or 3-speed Turbo Hydra-Matic automatics.
In the 1979 Z28, the 350-cubic-inch V8 was standard equipment, breathing through a four-barrel Quadrajet carburetor to generate 175 horsepower at 4,000 rpm and 270 pound-feet of torque at 2,400 rpm in federal trim. Low, but what could you ask from the dead of the Malaise? (Pontiac’s ruffian, the Trans Am, also got the upper hand in performance figures, with 220 hp and 320 lb-ft, courtesy of its W72-code 400-cuber).
Photo: YouTube/Always More To Do With a curb weight of roughly 3,580 pounds, an 8.2:1 compression ratio, and a front-disc and rear-drum braking configuration, the Z28 was the most spirited Chevrolet outside the Corvette. Contemporary instrumented tests recorded a 0 to 60 mph acceleration sprint of 7.3 seconds, a quarter-mile run of 16.0 seconds, and a top speed of 129 mph. It was a crushing fall from the great Z/28s of the past, considering that a particular example (Little Hoss) of 1967 was rated at 11.75 (in AHRA track suit, admittedly).
This brings us to a remarkable survivor featured by Scott Lofton on his YouTube channel Always More To Do . The vehicle is a pristine, garage-kept 1979 Chevrolet Camaro Z28 finished in brown with aftermarket wheels. What makes this example extraordinary is its provenance: it has been cherished by a single owner who purchased it brand-new off the dealer showroom floor in 1979 and kept it protected indoors ever since.
Throughout decades of ownership, this owner meticulously refined the sports coupe. Upgrades were not installed in one rapid spending spree; rather, improvements were executed gradually as personal finances and disciplined savings permitted over many years.
Photo: YouTube/Always More To Do Scott walked us through these mechanical revisions, noting how the owner patiently personalized the vehicle. The modifications transformed the late-second-generation F-body into a more capable, muscular street machine without compromising its period character.
Under the air-grabbing hood scoop, the original 350-cubic-inch small-block V8 received a comprehensive top-end overhaul. The cylinder heads were ported and polished to enhance airflow, matched by a ported aluminum high-rise intake manifold.
Fuel and air delivery were upgraded via a stout Rochester Quadrajet carburetor originally specified for the 454-cubic-inch big-block truck engine. Scavenging was improved with Cyclone exhaust headers, breathing deeper than any factory catalytic-choked setup.
Photo: YouTube/Always More To Do Beneath the chassis, the owner addressed the classic pony car handling dynamics. The front sway bar was enlarged from 1.25 inches to 1.5 inches, while the rear bar grew from 5/8 inch to 7/8 inch. Aftermarket front control arms were fitted alongside rigid plastic suspension bushings that completely replaced the compliant, squishy factory rubber units. To sharpen steering response, the factory 70-series tires mounted on 7-inch rims were swapped for wider 235/60R15 rubber.
Because that tire diameter alteration changed the rolling circumference and caused the mechanical speedometer to read significantly slower than actual vehicle speed—registering 75 mph when traveling closer to 82 mph—the rear axle was addressed. The owner swapped the original 3.40:1 ring-and-pinion gearing down to a 2.92:1 rear-end ratio.
This modification not only corrected speedometer accuracy back toward normal parameters, but also relaxed engine revolutions during sustained highway cruising.
Photo: YouTube/Always More To Do Scott welcomed the survivor into his shop for a comprehensive deep-cleaning and paint correction preservation. Because the Camaro spent its entire existence parked indoors away from wet road grime and harsh weather, the exterior had never suffered aggressive wash damage.
The factory black lacquer finish was completely free of severe swirl marks and deep gouging, allowing the detailer to skip heavy abrasive compounding entirely in favor of fine polishing and protective carnauba waxing.
Working around the iconic split front fascia, pointed nose, and trunk lid, Scott applied a double coat of polish across all horizontal body surfaces to maximize depth and gloss clarity, followed by another two coats of protective wax.
Photo: YouTube/Always More To Do The trunk revealed its untouched past, including the factory tire instruction decal, the unused original bumper jack, and the original collapsible space-saver spare tire paired with its unpierced factory inflation canister, serving as an authentic snapshot of late-seventies assembly line engineering.
The ultimate charm of this 1979 Z28 lies beyond its ported intake runners or upgraded anti-roll bars. When the detailing was completed and the long-time owner arrived alongside his wife to retrieve the gleaming machine, the emotional gravity of 47 years of shared memories surfaced. It’s not something EV owners of the 2020s will ever say in 2073. I suspect even car nuts who buy new combustion cars now won’t keep them until then, either.
